reference.title: Barbell Front Chest Squat
reference.listing: Video (title and product number from the listing URL; the page itself could not be read from this environment, so the movement follows the exercise name and standard coaching)

breathing.pattern: Big breath in and brace at the top, hold it on the way down and through the bottom, breathe out as you pass the hardest part of the rise.
breathing.cadence: About 2 s down, a short pause, about 1.2 s up

prescription.load: Barbell load is user-chosen: usually about 80-85% of your back squat. Leave about 2-3 reps in reserve (RPE 7-8).
prescription.progression: Add 2.5 kg when every rep reaches full depth with the elbows staying up.

cues.text: Bar across the front of the shoulders against the throat, fingertips under the bar just outside the shoulders, elbows high and forward. Step back, feet about shoulder width, toes out a little.
Brace and sit straight down between the heels, elbows up, chest tall, knees forward and out.
Hips below the knees, elbows still high, back flat.
Drive up leading with the elbows and chest; breathe out as you pass the hardest part.

mistakes.mistake: Elbows dropping so the bar rolls forward
mistakes.fix: Lead with the elbows: think of pushing them up to the ceiling as you rise.

mistakes.mistake: Holding the bar with the palms instead of resting it on the shoulders
mistakes.fix: Let the bar sit on the front delts; the fingers only keep it in place.
Lighter bar; keep the chest tall and the upper back tight.
Keep the whole foot down; work on ankle mobility or use lifting shoes.

kinematics.norm: About hip to shoulder width, toes out about 20-30 degrees (Lorenzetti 2018)
Less hip flexion than a back squat at the same depth (Gullett 2009)
More upright than a back squat (Gullett 2009)
Bar on the front delts against the throat, elbows high (common coaching)
Controlled, about 2 s down and 1-1.5 s up (clinical opinion)

sources.title: GymVisual, Barbell Front Chest Squat, video (movement reference only)
Gullett, Tillman, Gutierrez & Chow 2009, a biomechanical comparison of back and front squats in healthy trained individuals (J Strength Cond Res 23(1):284-292; PubMed 19002072)
Straub and Powers 2024, a biomechanical review of the squat exercise: implications for clinical practice (Int J Sports Phys Ther)
Lorenzetti et al. 2018, how to squat: stance widths, foot angles and experience (BMC Sports Sci Med Rehabil)

cautions: Squat inside a rack with the safety arms set just below your bottom position; to bail, push the bar forward off the shoulders and step back.
Wrist or elbow discomfort in the rack: widen the grip or let only two fingers hold the bar.
Stop if sharp pain, numbness, tingling or giving-way occurs.
Muscle glow colours and activation curves are illustrative, not measured EMG.
modify: Limited wrist mobility: a wider grip, or straps around the bar.
Knee pain: squat to a box at a pain-free depth.
progressions: Barbell clean into a front squat.

muscleNotes.quads_r: Main movers: the front rack keeps the trunk upright and the knees forward, with knee extensor demand similar to a back squat at a lighter load (Gullett 2009).
muscleNotes.quads_l: Main movers: the front rack keeps the trunk upright and the knees forward, with knee extensor demand similar to a back squat at a lighter load (Gullett 2009).
muscleNotes.glute_max_r: Extends the hip out of the bottom of the squat.
muscleNotes.glute_max_l: Extends the hip out of the bottom of the squat.
muscleNotes.adductors_r: Help extend the hip from the bottom.
muscleNotes.adductors_l: Help extend the hip from the bottom.
muscleNotes.hamstrings_r: Assist hip extension; their length changes little in a squat.
muscleNotes.hamstrings_l: Assist hip extension; their length changes little in a squat.
muscleNotes.spinal_extensors_r: Hold the upper back upright so the bar does not roll forward; less compressive load than a back squat (Gullett 2009).
muscleNotes.spinal_extensors_l: Hold the upper back upright so the bar does not roll forward; less compressive load than a back squat (Gullett 2009).
muscleNotes.calves_r: Control the forward travel of the knees over the planted feet.
muscleNotes.calves_l: Control the forward travel of the knees over the planted feet.
muscleNotes.core: Bracing stiffens the trunk under the bar.
muscleNotes.glute_med_r: Keeps the knees tracking over the feet.
muscleNotes.glute_med_l: Keeps the knees tracking over the feet.
muscleNotes.upper_traps_r: Raise the shoulders to make the shelf the bar rests on.
muscleNotes.upper_traps_l: Raise the shoulders to make the shelf the bar rests on.
muscleNotes.rhomboids_midtrap_r: Keep the upper back tight and upright under the bar.
muscleNotes.rhomboids_midtrap_l: Keep the upper back tight and upright under the bar.
muscleNotes.lats_r: Pull the bar down into the back and keep the upper back tight.
muscleNotes.lats_l: Pull the bar down into the back and keep the upper back tight.
muscleNotes.forearm_flexors_r: Fingers hold the bar in place on the shoulders.
muscleNotes.forearm_flexors_l: Fingers hold the bar in place on the shoulders.
muscleNotes.ant_deltoid_r: The front of the shoulders forms the shelf; holds the elbows up.
muscleNotes.ant_deltoid_l: The front of the shoulders forms the shelf; holds the elbows up.

phases.label: Stand tall, bar on the upper back
